title: Maximize the Minimum Game Score
summary: Given an array points of size n and an integer m, initialize an array gameScore of size n with all elements set to 0.
statement: Given an array points of size n and an integer m, initialize an array gameScore of size n with all elements set to 0. Starting from an index outside the array, make at most m moves to either increment or decrement the index by 1, adding points[i] to gameScore[i] at each move. Ensure the index stays within array bounds. The goal is to maximize the minimum value in gameScore after the moves.
constraints: points contains 2–50,000 positive values and m is a positive move limit.
Start immediately before index zero; each move goes to an adjacent in-bounds index and adds that index’s points to its score.
Using at most m moves, maximize the minimum score across all indices.
reference_solution:
def maximize_minimum_game_score(points,m):
    def feasible(target):
        used=carry=0
        for index,value in enumerate(points):
            visits=max(0,(target+value-1)//value-carry)
            used+=(2*visits-1 if visits else 0) if index==len(points)-1 else (2*visits-1 if visits else 1)
            if used>m:return False
            carry=max(0,visits-1)
        return True
    low=0;high=max(points)*m+1
    while low+1<high:
        middle=(low+high)//2
        if feasible(middle):low=middle
        else:high=middle
    return low

hints: Feasibility of reaching a target minimum is monotone, enabling binary search.
Sweep left to right, greedily add the visits still needed after credits from prior back-and-forth moves.
At an interior index, each added visit costs a round trip except the final step onward; carry the induced visits to the next index.
Delaying a missing visit cannot help once an index is left, so the minimum-move greedy count exactly characterizes feasibility.
